newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh govt urges farmers to harvest grain fast.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh govt urges farmers to harvest grain fast.

text.p: Kazakhstan's government has urged farmers to bring in the rest of this year's grain harvest as quickly as possible to avoid losses due to expected early snow, the official daily Kazakhstanskaya Pravda said.
A cabinet meeting on Wednesday described the harvest as "tense but inspiring hope for the successful carrying out of field work and stocking of feed supplies".

"Unsettled weather in September is leaving very little time for harvesting. In the last 10 days of the month, rain is expected to turn to snow. The government noted that every hour of fair weather has to be used," Kazakhstanskaya Pravda said.
The newspaper's account of the meeting gave no harvest forecast. The government has previously forecast the 1996 harvest at 16.5 million tonnes, well up on last year's disastrous 10 million tonnes.
But analysts in the northern grain belt have predicted output of 18-19 million tonnes.

Kazakhstansakaya Pravda said harvesting had been completed in southern regions and more than two-thirds of the crop had already been threshed in the Kustanai region in the breadbasket north of the country.
But only 25-40 percent of the area sown to grain had been threshed so far in other central and northern regions -- Akmola, Zhezkazgan, Kokshetau, Pavlodar, North-Kazakhstan and Turgai.
"Grain harvesting is going at an unacceptable slow pace in the Karaganda region where only 17 percent of the crop has been gathered," it added.

Kazakh farmers are not experiencing the severe shortages of fuel that have plagued previous harvests, but some have complained about inadequate supplies of combine harvesters, tractors and other equipment.

Kazakhstanskaya Pravda said preparations for next year's crop were under way. Farmers in the Kustanai region had stored more than half of the high-quality seed required, but the government described preparations in other regions as unsatisfactory.
